mechanism_narrative: The consistent week-on-week increase in RETAIL_REC mobility over the past four weeks indicates a sustained recovery trend, which is expected to continue and drive further increases in retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean over the last 28 days, indicating a reversal of the observed upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained return to workplaces, evidenced by WORKPLACES mobility remaining above -20% from baseline for two consecutive weeks, signals increased weekday foot traffic and associated retail spending, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES mobility exceeds -20% from baseline for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility remains above -20% for two consecutive weeks, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase compared to the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The combined trend of decreasing time spent at home (RESIDENTIAL), increasing public transit use (TRANSIT), and a return to offices (WORKPLACES) signifies a broad shift in daily routines towards out-of-home activities, collectively boosting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days, despite RESIDENTIAL continuing to decrease, and TRANSIT and WORKPLACES continuing to increase.

mechanism_narrative: The observed recovery in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility suggests an underlying easing of public health restrictions or a shift in policy, which will continue to encourage out-of-home activities and drive RETAIL_REC upwards over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days, even if TRANSIT and WORKPLACES continue their recovery, implying the policy shift did not translate to retail activity.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility over the past four weeks indicates a sustained behavioral shift towards spending less time at home, directly translating to more opportunities for retail and recreation, thus increasing RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility continues its downward trend, but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 14 days compared to the previous 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week increase in TRANSIT mobility of at least 3 percentage points indicates a significant surge in people moving around the metropolitan area, which will immediately translate into higher RETAIL_REC in the subsequent week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT mobility increases by at least 3 percentage points week-on-week
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility increases by 3 or more percentage points week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC declines or remains flat in the following week.

mechanism_narrative: The recent recovery in PARKS mobility, combined with the ongoing upward trend in RETAIL_REC, suggests a broader increase in leisure and discretionary outdoor activities, which will mutually reinforce and drive RETAIL_REC higher over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: PARKS mobility increases or remains stable, but RETAIL_REC declines over the next 14 days, indicating a decoupling of outdoor leisure from retail activity.

mechanism_narrative: The collective movement of RETAIL_REC, WORKPLACES, and RESIDENTIAL mobility towards pre-baseline levels signifies a strong post-lockdown recovery behavioral regime, where people are actively resuming normal activities, leading to a sustained increase in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: Despite WORKPLACES continuing to increase and RESIDENTIAL continuing to decrease, RETAIL_REC fails to show an overall increase over the next 28 days, suggesting a stagnation in the recovery regime.
